body:
N-27 SLICES 2c, 2b, 2e, 2d: ONE DESIGN, PART 1 OF 2 (lead, 14 Nov 2026 night; before any code, for the advisor).

THE PROBLEM. Slice 2a never retires a ref that once held a file (file_history): the only way a phone that was away learns that a song is gone is the files feed, which lists a ref that still exists (library.files_since skips a ref that is gone). The refs of deleted playlists and of imports are not retirable either (tombstoned entries and import_entry rows are pointers). Both are ONE gap: the server cannot say "this id is gone" to a phone. Close it once, with the precedent it already has: ref_merge (a tiny never-purged table, its own cursor, the phone opts in, an old phone is unchanged).

2c (SERVER, additive): a tombstone for retired refs.
* A migration that adds a table only: ref_gone(seq INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT, ref_id TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, at INTEGER NOT NULL); no foreign key (the ref no longer exists); never purged (about 60 bytes a row; a phone back after a year still hears it, as with ref_merge).
* The janitor writes one ref_gone row for EVERY ref it retires (junk too: a phone may hold a row from a tap on it), in the SAME transaction as the delete, and deletes the file_log rows of those refs (no foreign key; the feed skips them anyway).
* GET /library/files?goneSince=<cursor> adds gone: [{id, seq}], goneCursor, goneMore (paged like merges). WITHOUT the parameter nothing is added: an old phone parses every refs entry as a full ref and stays unchanged. A feature string `ref-gone` in info.features, so a phone never tries a route to find out. docs/17: one paragraph beside "Songs merged into another".
* The janitor keeps file_history in 2c: 2c only makes the server ABLE to tell.

2b (PHONE): applies it.
* When info.features has ref-gone, pullFiles sends goneSince (its own sync_state key like encoreMergesCursor; reset() clears it) and, in the SAME transaction as the page, for the ids in gone: clears the server-file link of the row (file_id = NULL: a stale file of a song that is gone), then calls the existing dropUnused, which already refuses a row with a like, a playlist entry or a download.
* That is the whole phone rule: NO age rule and NO widening of the feed. The earlier sketch ("older than 14 days and absent from every feed page") is dropped: an exact signal beats a guess. A row the person is looking at is an entry, a download or a like, all guarded; a queue holding a gone song plays through the tap-resolve path (the phone describes the song by name), as for any song the server cannot find.
* Edges that stay: an outbox edit naming a gone ref and a failed download retried after the ref is gone get a typed 404 (NotFoundFailure, said in words).
